rule: "Q-model supported" only if, on real data, the best Q-model beats the best classical baseline on split (b) by held-out NLL with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero, at matched or lower parameter count, and the interference-term CI excludes zero. Otherwise the conclusion is "no evidence of a quantum-probability advantage in the available data", and the report names the data that would resolve it. The dashboard serves whichever model wins on held-out NLL; if that is a classical model, the screen says so.
verdict: no evidence of a quantum-probability advantage in the available data
